reading.text:
Reading of spec ex_expfunc_jump (Example 5.3, last paragraph: the Li-Min jump coefficient
"embeds instead through the Nemytskii map [H_t(theta,theta')](e) := hbar(t,x,y,z,u(e),
x',y',z',u'(e),e) for nu-a.e. e. This map is again well defined on equivalence classes. Assume
it jointly Borel, and impose ... |H_t(th1,th1') - H_t(th2,th2')|_{L^2(nu)} <= C(|th1-th2|_H +
|th1'-th2'|_H), int_0^T |H_t(0,0)|^2 dt < infinity, so that H_t is Lipschitz into
L^2(nu;R^n) and (2.10) applies, with that space in the role of K, to h(t,theta,mu) :=
int_H H_t(theta, theta') mu(dtheta')").

Setting: standing H = R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x L^2(nu;R^m), sigma-finite nu (Li-Min:
finite activity, but the paragraph's conclusion does not use finiteness), horizon T.
Data: hbar : [0,T] x R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x R^m x R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x R^m x E -> R^n; its
Nemytskii map H_t : H x H -> L^2(nu;R^n), assumed well defined (the composite e |-> hbar(...,
u(e), ..., u'(e), e) lies in L^2(nu) and its class does not depend on the representatives of
u, u'), jointly Borel, with
 (L) |H_t(th1,th1') - H_t(th2,th2')| <= C(|th1-th2|_H + |th1'-th2'|_H) for all t, th's;
 (I) int_0^T |H_t(0,0)|^2_{L^2(nu)} dt < infinity.
Conclusion: h(t,theta,mu) := int_H H_t(theta,theta') mu(dtheta') (Bochner, in L^2(nu;R^n)) is
well defined for mu in P_2(H) and the law-dependence component of Assumption 2.4 holds by
(2.10): |h(t,theta,mu) - h(t,theta,mu')|_{L^2(nu)} <= C W_2(mu,mu') (constant Lip(H_t(theta,.))
<= C). The fuller reading (the paragraph's "embeds", i.e. h is an admissible jump coefficient)
adds |h(t,th1,mu) - h(t,th2,mu)| <= C|th1-th2|_H and the origin integrability
h(.,0,delta_0) = H_.(0,0) in L^2(0,T;L^2(nu)), and Borel measurability (2.4). A faithful
statement must contain at least the W_2-Lipschitz conclusion with constant C; including the
state-Lipschitz and origin parts is fine. If the Lean takes H_t abstractly (any map into
L^2(nu;R^n) with (L),(I)), that is broader than the Nemytskii instance and fine, as long as
the Nemytskii map of an hbar is an instance (the well-definedness on classes is then a
separate matter; the paper asserts it).
Norm conventions: |.|_H the l^2 product norm; W_2 on P_2(H) w.r.t. it.

comparison.text:
Comparison, ex_expfunc_jump (Sec5.lean:402-431).
Setting: sigma-finite nu on countably generated E, n m d, hbar : R -> B -> B -> E -> R^n on the
blocks B = R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x R^m (pointwise values (x,y,z,u(e))) - the printed kernel
hbar(t,x,y,z,u(e),x',y',z',u'(e),e).
Part 1 (well defined on equivalence classes): for all t, theta, theta' and representatives v, v'
a.e. equal to the u-channels, the Nemytskii composite with v, v' agrees nu-a.e. with the one with
the canonical representatives. Present ("This map is again well defined on equivalence
classes").
Part 2: forall H : R -> H -> H -> L^2(nu;R^n) representing the Nemytskii map (H t th th' =ae
the composite), forall C >= 0 with |H t th1 th1' - H t th2 th2'| <= C(|th1-th2|_H + |th1'-th2'|_H)
(Hilbert norm via toL2 - printed), then for all t, theta, mu, mu' in P2(H):
|int H t theta . dmu - int H t theta . dmu'| <= C w2H mu mu' - (2.10) with K = L^2(nu;R^n),
Lip(H_t(theta, .)) <= C, W_2 of the Hilbert norm. Present.
Differences from the printed passage:
 - the hypotheses "jointly Borel" and (I) int_0^T |H_t(0,0)|^2 dt < infinity are not assumed;
   the law-Lipschitz conclusion does not use them (broader);
 - H is quantified as any L^2(nu)-valued map representing the Nemytskii map instead of being
   defined as its class; the printed passage assumes the map lands in L^2(nu;R^n), so such an H
   exists (the class) and is unique; a representation choice;
 - t ranges over R instead of [0,T] (broader);
 - the conclusion is the law-dependence component (2.10) only, which is what the passage says
   ("(2.10) applies ... to h"); the state-Lipschitz/origin parts I listed as optional.
Instantiation giving the printed claim: take the paper's hbar with its Nemytskii map Lipschitz
into L^2(nu;R^n) with constant C (and (I), Borel - unused), H := its L^2 class.
Witness ex_expfunc_jump_hypotheses: hbar = x - x' at nu = delta_0 with its class H, Lipschitz -
an instance of the Li-Min finite-activity class. Fine.
Verdict: broader.

verdict.detail:
Broader than printed. The Lean (part 2) assumes only that H represents the Nemytskii map in
L^2(nu;R^n) and is C-Lipschitz for the Hilbert norm; it drops the printed hypotheses "jointly
Borel" and int_0^T |H_t(0,0)|^2 dt < infinity, which the law-Lipschitz conclusion (2.10) does not
use, and lets t range over R. Instantiation giving the printed claim: the paper's hbar whose
Nemytskii map lands in L^2(nu;R^n), with H := its L^2 class (which then represents it), the
Lipschitz constant C, and the extra (unused) Borel and origin hypotheses; the conclusion
|h(t,theta,mu) - h(t,theta,mu')| <= C W_2(mu,mu') is the printed one. Representation choice: H is
quantified as any representative map rather than defined as the class (they coincide).

author_review.disagreements: The author's review recorded for this unit is empty (its text is attached to an adjacent review marker of a unit outside this chunk and was not shown), so there is nothing to compare point by point. My verdict: broader - the proposition drops the printed hypotheses 'jointly Borel' and int_0^T |H_t(0,0)|^2 dt < infinity and quantifies over any L^2-valued representative H of the Nemytskii map; the printed claim is its instance.
